podcast.body: A "quirky single" that reached the top spot during The Beatles' second imperial phase in America, which spanned from 1967 through 1968, demonstrating their continued ability to score number one hits. "with even quirky singles, like All You Need is Love, and Hello Goodbye, Reaching the Top Spot."

podcast.body: The orchestral arrangement for this Beatles track, produced by George Martin, incorporated elements from Glenn Miller's big band hit "In the Mood," leading to a claim against Martin for unauthorized use. "Back in 1967, George Martin, a famous producer of most of the Beatles work, got nailed for using elements of Glenn Miller's big band hit in the mood for the orchestral arrangement of the Beatles track All You Need Is Love."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This song was recorded at Olympic Studios for The Beatles' 1968 satellite broadcast. "This is where the Beatles recorded all you need as love for their 1968 satellite broadcast."
